pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Guided Writing
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why is writing legibly and neatly important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. write simple words and phrases legibly and neatly
2. show awareness of the importance of writing legibly for effective communication
3. apply punctuation rules accurately in written texts

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Guided Writing

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Guided Writing

Teach
• Focus skill: write simple words and phrases legibly and neatly.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Guided Writing.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Guided Writing
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is writing legibly and neatly important?
2. how a proper diet is important for wellness. Why should we punctuate written texts clearly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
